misconceptions.description: Equating a visually polished or on-time submission with a publication-ready package that another designer could rebuild and reuse
misconceptions.trigger: learner judges readiness by appearance, size, or deadline rather than by whether an outsider could reproduce the artifact's use
misconceptions.feedback: Test the package for reuse: can a competent stranger find the canonical files and reproduce the work from the package alone?

misconceptions.description: Publishing reused materials, or AI-assisted components, without source, license, attribution, or verification notes
misconceptions.trigger: learner includes stock media, a colleague's rubric, or AI output with no provenance recorded
misconceptions.feedback: Record source, license, attribution, and how AI-assisted parts were verified. Provenance is part of the publishable package.

misconceptions.description: Bundling many files with no manifest or README that names the canonical artifact and the steps to run or read it
misconceptions.trigger: package has no index distinguishing the final files or explaining how to use the prototype
misconceptions.feedback: Add a manifest and README that name the canonical files and the steps to run them, so a reviewer is not left guessing.
